name: Meadowmark
headline: The Meadowmark is a 200-home affordable community for adults 55 and older at 3223 Timber Mill Parkway in The Meadows neighborhood of Castle Rock, developed by Ulysses Development Group; it won $3,091,143 a year in 2022 federal 4% credit with bonds issued by the Douglas County Housing Partnership, opened to residents in December 2024 and held its grand opening on 2025-04-30.
why_it_matters: It shows a county housing partnership using its own bond issuing power to finance the largest senior affordable property in Douglas County, with a DOLA loan and a Freddie Mac permanent loan in the stack.

status.label: Open: residents moving in from December 2024; grand opening 2025-04-30; 8609s not yet issued
status.detail: Ground broke 2023-06-13; the developer announced first move-ins on 2024-12-11 and held a grand opening on 2025-04-30, and Mission Rock Residential now markets the property. CHFA still lists it on its 2026-09-21 award report, which excludes developments with 8609s issued.

next_step: Watch for 8609 issuance, when the deal moves to CHFA's 4% completed developments report.

key_numbers.meaning: 10 units at 30% AMI, 167 at 60% and 23 at 70%; 130 one-bedrooms and 70 two-bedrooms.
About $30.9M over 10 years (inferred); the developer reports $28.8M of credit equity from Raymond James.
Revenue Notes (The Meadowmark Project) Series 2023, $34,849,421; CHFA's report shows $34,465,000.

key_numbers.value: $6M from DOLA; $31.3M Freddie Mac permanent loan
key_numbers.meaning: Other pieces named at the grand opening.

facts.value: 3223 Timber Mill Parkway, Castle Rock (northeast corner of Timber Mill Parkway and North Meadows Drive); CHFA lists Meadows Filing 19, Lot 2, North Parcel D2A, zip 80109

Mission Rock advertises one-bedrooms from $999 and two-bedrooms from $1,165 with two months free annualized

background.text: It was Ulysses Development Group's first Colorado project; the developer called it the third-largest senior affordable community built in metro Denver in the previous ten years and the largest in Douglas County.

The Douglas County Housing Partnership issued the tax-exempt notes for the acquisition, construction and equipping of the property, so the bond cap came through the county partnership rather than CHFA's pool (inferred from the issuer named).
The groundbreaking forecast a 20-month build and opening in early 2025; first residents moved in in December 2024, a little ahead of that.
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2022 Round One or Round Two competitive application narratives; it was a rolling 4% bond deal only.

CHFA's 4% award report says it leaves out developments whose IRS Form 8609s have been issued; this deal is still listed on the 2026-09-21 report, so 8609s had not been issued by then (inferred from the report's note).

timeline.event: Douglas County Housing Partnership issues $34,849,421 of Revenue Notes, Series 2023 (announced 2023-04-25)
Mission Rock Residential selected as property manager
Still listed on CHFA's Federal 4% award report (no 8609s yet)

discrepancies.text: The bond amount is $34,465,000 in CHFA's award report, $34,849,421 in the bond counsel's notice and $34.89 million in the grand opening release.
